name: Offer change-approval gate (executing → awaiting_approval)
description:
First human gate. When a run's generated OpenSpec change has been authored and blessed by the CLI validator (openspec.change.validated present) but no human approval exists yet (run.change.decision absent — the gate is undecided), move the run to awaiting_approval so the dev loop cannot start. This encodes the validate-before-approval ordering (G-io task 4.4/3.7): approval is only offered after the change is OpenSpec-valid. The transition is rule-owned (G2) — no product Go fires it. CONTRACT (design D15): this rule evaluates conditions against the RUN entity, so group 4's validate harness MUST stamp openspec.change.validated on the run entity (subject = agent.run.entity-id), not on the loop or a change entity, or this rule never fires and the run wedges silently.

CONTENT-FRESHNESS DEFERRED (design D15 forward-contract #0): ideally this gate would require openspec.change.validated to EQUAL the run's current content revision, so a rework re-author cannot reach the human gate on a stale validation. That needs a slug-independent field-to-field compare, but the only engine form ($entity.triple.<pred> in a condition value) floods a 'likely silent-pass bug' WARN on every entity that lacks the predicate (semstreams #519). At M0 the hazard is UNREACHABLE — no live path re-authors a change while the run is executing (no awaiting_approval→executing rework path yet) — so presence-only is safe here. The REACHABLE guard lives in project_tasks (Go, warn-free: it freezes task.spec only when openspec.change.validated == openspec.change.<slug>.revision). When a rework path lands, this gate MUST adopt the content-freshness compare (via the engine fix or the .triples form) — pinned by TestChangeApprovalGateFreshnessForwardContract and design D15 #0.

on_enter.reason: change authored and OpenSpec-validated; awaiting human change approval
